question: How can historians measure how long English people worked before anyone kept time sheets?
answer: From criminal trials. Witnesses at the Old Bailey often said what they had been doing, and when, as a crime happened. Hans-Joachim Voth pooled such remarks to rebuild the working year: by 1800 Londoners worked about 3,300 hours, as holy days and the habit of skipping Monday faded away.
move: When no one recorded something, look for records made for another purpose.
source: Voth, Time and Work in England, 2000
reference: Voth, Time and Work in England 1750–1830, Clarendon Press, 2000
